newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WIN TOSS, ELECT TO BAT VS W INDIES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-AUSTRALIA WIN TOSS, ELECT TO BAT VS W INDIES.

text.p: Australian captain Mark Taylor won the toss and elected to bat in a World Series limited overs match against The West Indies at the WACA ground on Sunday.
Australia, who are at the bottom of the table in the tri-nation series, must win this match if they are to have any hope of making the finals of the series later this month.
Australia, who have lost their last five international matches in a row, have not missed a place in the their annual international limited overs series since 1979/80.
Conversely, The West Indies lead the competition with four wins from six games and are virtually assured of a place in the finals series regardless of the result of this game.

The West Indies drafted strike fast bowler Curtly Ambrose back into the side after one game off with a hamstring strain. He replaces Patterson Thompson who played in the West Indies' win over Pakistan in Perth on Friday.

Australia have kept all but one of their side which lost a low scoring match against Pakistan on Tuesday. Free-swinging batsman and medium pace bowler Tom Moody replaces new paceman Anthony Stuart, who is 12th man.

West Indies - Sherwin Campbell, Junior Murray, Shivnarine Chanderpaul, Brian Lara, Carl Hooper, Jimmy Adams, Robert Samuels, Curtly Ambrose, Ian Bishop, Adrian Griffith, Courtney Walsh (captain), Roland Holder (12th man).
Australia - Mark Taylor (captain), Mark Waugh, Stuart Law, Steve Waugh, Michael Bevan, Greg Blewett, Ian Healey, Shane Warne, Andrew Bichel, Glenn McGrath, Tom Moody, Anthony Stuart (12th man).
